solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: He's been removed from dictionary, the beast

indicators.note: something that has been removed from a word is taken out of it, so these letters leave the longer word

parts.note: a thesaurus is a dictionary of synonyms, loosely a dictionary
the letters of he's, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A man has been struck out of a dictionary, leaving only some animal behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove HES from THESAURUS and TAURUS is left: the bull of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: Taurus is the bull, the animal of the zodiac sign and constellation, so it is a fair beast.

clue.text: Precedent established over EEC stats

indicators.note: over suggests turning things over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ruling sets a precedent on European Economic Community statistics.
explanation.walkthrough: EEC was the European Economic Community, the forerunner of the EU.
explanation.definitionFit: A test case is a legal action whose outcome sets a precedent for later cases.

clue.text: Modest girl's rest I've disturbed

parts.note: Una is a girl's name, with the S of the possessive

indicators.note: letters that are disturbed are moved around into a new order

parts.note: the letters of I've, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A demure girl's rest has been disturbed, she says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges REST into SERT; Una is a girl's name, and the S comes from the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unassertive does not push themselves forward, so they are modest or meek.

clue.text: How Mr Lyttleton contained his doubt

definitions.text: How Mr Lyttleton contained his doubt

parts.words: How Mr Lyttleton contained his doubt
parts.note: the British jazz trumpeter Lyttelton went by a nickname that is also a grunt of doubt; holding back its opening aitch leaves the entry

explanation.walkthrough: Lyttelton was a British jazz trumpeter and radio host whose short first name doubles as a sceptical grunt; 'contained' means he kept its initial H to himself.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a variant of the grunt humph, a sound expressing doubt or mild disapproval.

clue.text: Flower water put in sticky paste

indicators.note: one thing put in another is placed inside it
a sticky situation is awkward, hinting that the letters of paste are in a mess and rearranged

parts.note: wee is an informal word for urine, water passed

explanation.surface: A gardener mixes a flower with water into a gluey paste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sticky' rearranges PASTE into STPEA. 'Flower' looks like a river here, but it is the plain bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet pea is a climbing garden plant grown for its scented blooms.

clue.text: Clean up place where dust fills a wide area

indicators.note: what fills something goes inside it

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide
room means space or area
ash is the dust left by burning

explanation.surface: A big space gets covered in dust, so it is time for a clean-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clean up place' reads as an instruction to tidy; it is the definition, a room for washing in.
explanation.definitionFit: A washroom is a room with basins and toilets where people clean themselves.

clue.text: Environmentalist fight for 2016 Olympics run by Coe — not well — initially

indicators.note: initially says that rearranged name goes at the start
something not well is out of sorts, so the letters of the name are reordered

parts.note: war is fighting
the 2016 Summer Olympics were held in Rio de Janeiro
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A campaigner battles over the Rio Games, which Sebastian Coe oversaw while unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not well' turns COE into ECO, which 'initially' puts at the front. Sebastian Coe is a British former runner who now runs World Athletics.
explanation.definitionFit: An eco-warrior is an activist who campaigns hard to protect the natural world.

clue.text: Tart is oddly pricey

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: A pastry that is strangely expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A tart is a pastry case with a filling, much like a pie.

clue.text: Agree to how it was issued

parts.note: as can mean how, in the manner in which
sent means dispatched or issued

explanation.surface: Someone signs off on a document exactly as it was sent out.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer's pieces as 'as sent', the way something was dispatched.
explanation.definitionFit: To assent is to agree to a proposal or give approval.

clue.text: Birds leaving Canada behind; it's a sign

indicators.note: something leaving a word goes out of it
behind says the letters go and are left behind, not kept

parts.note: canaries are small songbirds

explanation.surface: Some birds fly south from Canada, and it is an omen.
explanation.walkthrough: CAN comes off the front of CANARIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Aries the ram is the first sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Injure retreating salesman: run for it

parts.note: to scar is to injure, leaving a mark

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the word for the salesman is read in reverse

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: Someone hurts a door-to-door salesman and then flees the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns REP into PER. SCARPER is British slang for running away.
explanation.definitionFit: To scarper is a British slang verb meaning to flee or bolt away quickly.

clue.text: Washes over groups of slovenly people

definitions.meaning: takes quick baths under a spray of water
British slang calls a hopeless or useless bunch of people a shower

explanation.walkthrough: 'a right shower' is a British insult for an incompetent or disreputable group.
explanation.definitionFit: Showers are quick washes under spray, and in British slang a shower is a useless rabble.

clue.text: About to request a container

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
to ask is to request

explanation.surface: Someone wants to ask for a container to put something in.
explanation.definitionFit: A cask is a wooden barrel holding liquids such as beer or wine.

clue.text: King George is back in Aberdeen perhaps, finding somewhere to drink

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other, inside it
perhaps suggests the letters of the city name are only one possible arrangement
something that is back is turned round, so these two letters run backwards

parts.note: GR is the royal cipher Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: A Hanoverian monarch returns to a Scottish city and goes looking for a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the letters into BEEARDEN; 'is back' turns GR into RG. Aberdeen is a city in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A beer garden is an outdoor area at a pub where customers sit and have their pints.

clue.text: Dog-tired, Anna, having lost Pole, suffered humiliation

indicators.note: suffering puts things through hardship, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: N is the North Pole, the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: An exhausted woman named Anna, having lost a Polish friend, felt shamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost' removes one N from the letters of DOG-TIRED ANNA, and 'suffered' shuffles the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Degradation is the loss of dignity or self-respect, which is humiliation.

clue.text: Counter that Eastern Union needs time to start referendum

parts.note: NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, a British trade union
an era is a period of time
taken as written

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A census official says an eastern trade union needs time before a vote.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUM is the British miners' union.
explanation.definitionFit: An enumerator counts things, for example a census-taker counting households.

clue.text: Bound to start at the beginning

definitions.meaning: the first season of the year, when growth begins

explanation.walkthrough: Spring is a leap, and it is also the season that opens the growing year.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring is a leap, and spring is the season when the year's growth starts.

clue.text: Bravery shown when drunken plastic surgeon removes splints

indicators.note: a drunken person is muddled, so the letters of the phrase are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of these words are rearranged once the other word's letters are taken out
these letters are the ones taken away from the larger pool

explanation.surface: A tipsy cosmetic surgeon takes the splints off a patient and needs nerve to do it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removes' says the letters of SPLINTS come out of PLASTIC SURGEON; 'drunken' shuffles the seven letters left, A C U R G E O, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage is a synonym for bravery, the quality of facing danger or pain without fear.

clue.text: Example of fashionable point of view

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
a stance is an attitude or position

explanation.surface: A case study of the trendy point of view.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a case or single example of something.

clue.text: This hero takes the road followed by six Kings

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a road
Britain had six kings named George

explanation.surface: A hero takes the road, and six monarchs follow behind him.
explanation.walkthrough: St George is England's patron saint, the dragon-slayer.
explanation.definitionFit: St George, patron saint of England, is the legendary hero who slew a dragon.

clue.text: Small type of stone

definitions.meaning: an old name for a very small size of printing type, about four and a half point
a precious gem, here the hardest one

explanation.walkthrough: Printers once named type sizes; diamond was one of the smallest.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamond is a tiny printing type size and also the hardest gemstone.

clue.text: Movement that saw some take work in

indicators.note: to take something is to hold it, here within another piece
the word for work goes in the middle of the other piece

parts.note: part means some of something
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A movement that welcomed some people taking work home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' and 'in' together signal the insertion. Pop art is the 1950s-60s art movement built on mass-culture images.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop art was an art movement of the 1950s and 1960s drawing on advertising and comics.

clue.text: Premier English flower festival

indicators.note: premier means first, so the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: The best English flower show.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian festival celebrating the resurrection.

clue.text: Tricks SFO under pressure to hold old lecturer

indicators.note: something made to hold another piece has it inside
letters under pressure are squeezed into a new shape

explanation.surface: The Serious Fraud Office, under pressure, detains an elderly academic for deceptions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under pressure' rearranges SFO into FOS. The SFO is Britain's Serious Fraud Office.
explanation.definitionFit: To fool someone is to trick them, so the verb in its third-person form means tricks.

clue.text: Irregularity Lincoln's helping to hide, right?

indicators.note: something hidden is kept inside, so the letter for right sits within the pieces

parts.note: Abe is the first name of Abraham Lincoln
a ration is a helping or portion

explanation.surface: An odd query about Lincoln's share being kept secret, is that right?
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln's first name stands for the man himself; the question mark just softens the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An aberration is a departure from the normal course, an anomaly or quirk.

clue.text: Yes, Percy's first; first on duty

indicators.note: the second first says that letter goes at the front, before the word for yes
the first letter of the name is taken

parts.note: aye is an old or Scottish word for yes

explanation.surface: Percy gets the nod to go first, first on duty.
explanation.walkthrough: PAYE (Pay As You Earn) is the British system that takes income tax from wages; tax is a duty.
explanation.definitionFit: PAYE is the UK pay-as-you-earn income tax, and a tax may be called a duty.

clue.text: Introducing mobster's overtly lovely lady!

indicators.note: the letters that introduce each word are its first ones

explanation.surface: Meet the gangster's glamorous girlfriend!
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a picture of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A moll is a gangster's female companion.

clue.text: Attempt a fitting trick

definitions.meaning: put on a garment to see if it fits
British idiom for trying to deceive or chance one's luck with someone

explanation.walkthrough: In British English to 'try it on' is to attempt a cheeky deception.
explanation.definitionFit: Trying it on is both testing a garment for size and attempting a deceit to see if it works.

clue.text: Certainly polyester contains it

indicators.note: contains signals a word held inside the longer one

explanation.surface: Polyester certainly has it in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes affirms strongly, as certainly does in reply to a question.

clue.text: More crazy about the Opel Rio!

indicators.note: about here means round and round, so the letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is getting dottier about a little family car.
explanation.walkthrough: The Opel Rio is a car-like surface; Opel is a German carmaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Loopy is informal for mad, so the comparative means madder or more crazy.

clue.text: Taken to be unforthcoming

definitions.meaning: booked in advance, as a seat or table
quiet and slow to reveal feelings

explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is only a link between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved table is already taken, and a reserved person is shy and holds back.

clue.text: Take it when you're committed

parts.note: the idiom of taking a decisive step into something, said of a person who has made up their mind

explanation.walkthrough: To 'take the plunge' is to commit yourself to a bold course, such as marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A plunge is the leap you take in the idiom for finally committing to something bold.
